provenance.note: Structural engineering-chain facts for Greater Mumbai (BMC) water supply, anchored on BMC's own Hydraulic Engineer RTI manuals (Dec 2024) - Mumbai's equivalent of Chennai's ADB IEE - plus the MCGM O&M handbook, the 2018 24x7 White Paper and dated press for the expansion programme; per-section citations in the legacy _sources array. _view_overrides is a grandfathered UI hint (spec 6.4), config-migration follow-up on record.

_note: Structural at-a-glance facts for Greater Mumbai's (BMC) water supply engineering chain, compiled 2026-07 primarily from BMC's own RTI manuals - the Deputy Hydraulic Engineer (Bhandup Complex) manual and the Water Supply Projects department manual (both updated Dec 2024) - plus the MCGM-authored 'Water Supply Projects and Water Distribution System O&M' handbook (~2012, hosted at Somaiya CDEM), the 2018 'Toward Equitable and 24x7 Water Supply' White Paper (via ORF), and engineering press for the 2025-26 expansion programme. Mumbai has no ADB project document like Chennai/Madurai; the RTI manuals are the equivalent primary engineering source. current_supply_total_mld is the supplied figure (Praja 2024: 3,975 MLD; BMC's own draw statement is 3,850); the supply-mix rows are INSTALLED TREATMENT CAPACITY per stream, which is why they sum higher (~4,283 MLD incl. headroom). Connections are as on March 2025 (551,459; Praja RTI). Supply pairs by source: BMC's own ESR 2024-25 states 4,000 MLD supplied vs 4,505 demanded; Praja's 2024 audit says 3,975 vs 4,664; BMC's older draw statement is 3,850. Praja's Table 2 reconciles the chain: source yield ~4,370 MLD minus ~395 en-route losses = ~3,975 supplied.

_view_overrides.subtitle: Structural numbers from BMC's Hydraulic Engineer RTI manuals (Dec 2024), BMC's ESR 2024-25, the MCGM O&M handbook and the 2018 24x7 White Paper. Connections as on March 2025 (Praja RTI). Refreshed when new engineering documents are published.
_view_overrides.demand_caption: Mumbai's system is gravity from end to end bar one lift: lakes 65-160 km out feed Bhandup by gravity, one pump station raises treated water to hilltop balancing reservoirs, and gravity does the rest - which is why production cost stayed near Rs 12/KL. The strain is at both ends: demand projected at 6,424 MLD by 2041 (2018 White Paper; BMC's 2025 statements say ~6,535, and critics contest the 240-lpcd basis behind such projections), against ~3,975 MLD supplied today with ~34% non-revenue water. BMC's staged answer: Gargai +440 MLD, Manori desalination 200-400 MLD, Pinjal +865 MLD, Damanganga-Pinjal +1,586 MLD, and 1,232 MLD of tertiary treated-water reuse.

supply_chain: Seven lakes 65-160 km out in the Sahyadri foothills: Bhatsa, Upper + Middle Vaitarna, Modak Sagar, Tansa (gravity) + the in-city Vihar (1860, India's first piped scheme) and Tulsi (1885)

Four trunk mains into the city - 108" Upper Vaitarna, 96" Modak Sagar (76 km, 1957), 2 x 72" Tansa East/West - plus ~85 km of completed deep tunnels (5.5 m dia Gundavali-Kapurbawdi-Bhandup inlet, Maroshi-Ruparel, Amar Mahal-Trombay/Wadala-Parel commissioning 2026)
One raw-water lift - Pise weir pumps (1981, the system's first and only major pumping) via 2,235 mm rising mains to Panjrapur; clarified Bhatsa water injected into the Vaitarna mains at Yewai
Treatment: Bhandup Complex 2,810 MLD (1,910 MLD 1981 plant - Asia's largest at commissioning - plus 900 MLD 2014 plant) + Pise-Panjrapur 1,365 MLD + Vihar 90 + Tulsi 18 MLD
One treated-water lift at Bhandup (11 x 246 MLD pumps, 'the largest municipal pump house') to hilltop Master Balancing Reservoirs: Bhandup 246 ML + Middle Vaitarna 140 ML + Yewai 130 ML
Gravity from the MBRs to 27 service reservoirs, then to 109 water-supply zones
~650 km of transmission mains + ~5,500 km of distribution mains (80-1,800 mm), SCADA-controlled from Bhandup
At the tap: average 5.37 hours of supply a day (2024); only T ward (Mulund) gets 24x7

distribution._note: Mumbai's distribution differs from Madurai's OHT model: 3 hilltop Master Balancing Reservoirs (516 ML aggregate) feed 27 service reservoirs by gravity, which feed 109 intermittent water-supply zones. Connections are counted per BUILDING, not per household: one connection typically serves an entire society, chawl or slum cluster, which is why ~5.5 lakh connections supply a city of over 1.2 crore people (~23 people per connection). Bengaluru's plotted low-rise pattern yields far more connections per resident - connection counts are not comparable across cities.
distribution._connections_note: As on March 2025 (Praja May-2025 report, RTI Table 5): 529,123 metered + 22,336 unmetered. Replaces the ~2012 WDIP figure. Building-level connections, not households - one connection often serves a whole society or chawl.

demand._population_design_note: MCGM handbook projection for 2041 (16.57 million within BMC limits).
demand._demand_2034_note: Field name kept for tile-schema compatibility; the figure is the 2018 White Paper's 2041 projection (6,424 MLD). BMC's 2025 public statements cite ~6,535 MLD; Question of Cities contests the 240-lpcd norm behind these projections (its reading of BMC's figure: 5,940 MLD).
demand._demand_gap_note: 6,424 MLD (2041 projection) minus ~3,975 MLD supplied today. Separately, ~34% of today's supply is non-revenue water (~1,343 MLD) - close to the entire current supply-demand shortfall.
